signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Unwind
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades under heavy pressure as JPY emerges as the clear G10 leader with a 1W average of +2.303% against peers, while CAD lags at -0.867%. The resulting 3.170% leader-to-laggard spread signifies a powerful bilateral theme driven by a massive carry trade unwind, specifically impacting the +125bp CAD/JPY carry advantage. Despite the carry favor, JPY is supported by a strong Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +22.9, while CAD's neutral +3.4 index fails to provide a buffer against the selling. The options market is aggressively positioned for further JPY strength, with EUR/JPY 25d Risk Reversals at -2.93 and USD/JPY at -3.19 indicating a high premium for JPY calls. Technically, USD/JPY has broken below its SMA200 at 157.95, confirming a broader trend shift toward JPY. Risk: VIX remains below 20, allowing carry-seeking flows to re-enter and stabilize the CAD/JPY cross.

signals.title: USD/JPY — ISM Momentum + BoJ Intervention Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 156.88, having broken below its SMA200 (157.95) despite a surge in US macro data. July US ISM Manufacturing hit a three-year high of 55.6 (vs 54.0 expected), and the Atlanta Fed GDPNow estimate jumped to 6.2%, yet the pair remains unable to reclaim the 160.00 level that previously triggered verbal warnings. The options market shows extreme caution with a USD/JPY 25d Risk Reversal of -3.19, a strong put skew that signals traders are paying for downside protection against further BoJ tightening or intervention. Speculative positioning (COT) remains heavily short JPY (lev_net -124,575), creating a crowded trade that is vulnerable to further liquidation if 156.00 is tested. Carry still favors USD by +275bp, but momentum is currently dominated by position squaring. Risk: Fed-BoJ spread widens further on 16 Sep, forcing a re-test of the 160.00 ceiling.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Positioning vs CB Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5868, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5795–0.5826) as speculative positioning reaches a bearish extreme. COT LF net short is -30,606 with long positioning at only 9.7%, marking a deep spec fade against a central bank that is actively HIKING. This positioning extreme sits in direct opposition to a strong NZD Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +33.4 and an RBNZ hike bias for the 2 Sep meeting. The negative real policy rate of -1.56% for NZD suggests the RBNZ has significant room to tighten further to reach restrictive territory. If the 2 Sep meeting delivers a hawkish outcome, the crowded spec short is at risk of a rapid squeeze toward 0.6000. Risk: Oil prices continue to decline (WTI -5.85%), weighing on commodity-linked sentiment and validating the NZD short.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Volatility Risk Premium + Safe Haven
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8109, supported by a massive +375bp Fed-SNB carry advantage, yet options pricing indicates extreme tail-risk hedging. The pair's 1M Implied Volatility (IV) has spiked to 24.8% against a 30-day realized volatility (HV30) of only 6.5%, resulting in a massive Volatility Risk Premium (VRP) of +18.4%. This premium suggests the options market is pricing in a major volatility event or safe-haven CHF bid that has not yet manifested in spot price action. COT data shows specs are net short CHF (-11,635), but the 3.170% G10 spread suggests CAD and CHF are the primary underperformers this week. A sustained break back below the SMA20 (0.8106) would confirm that safe-haven demand is overwhelming the carry advantage. Risk: US-Iran negotiations result in a de-escalation, collapsing the VRP and supporting the carry-driven USD/CHF bid.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Technical Support + Carry Neutrality
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3427, currently holding just above its SMA20/50/200 cluster centered between 1.3365 and 1.3400. The pair is operating in a carry-neutral environment with a 0bp spread between Fed and BoE policy rates (3.75%), leaving direction dependent on macro data and positioning. GBP COT remains net long (+36,661), but retail sentiment has shifted to 65% short, creating a classic institutional-retail divergence. While the options market shows a mild put skew (25d RR -0.56), the elevated VRP of +4.9% suggests traders are paying for protection against a break of the moving average cluster. Failure to hold the 1.3365 SMA50 support would invalidate the current bullish structure. Risk: A dovish BoE shift on 17 Sep erodes the GBP real rate of +0.93%, triggering a long unwind.
